references.text: God promises Abraham that He will make him a great nation and that all the families of the earth shall be blessed through him – the original promise repeated throughout the patriarchal narrative.
God confirms His covenant with Abraham and promises that he will become the father of many nations, and that kings shall come from him.
After Abraham has passed the test with Isaac, God reaffirms the promise that all the families of the earth shall be blessed through his offspring.
Paul explains that Scripture foresaw that God would justify the Gentiles by faith, quoting the promise: "In you shall all the nations be blessed."
Peter reminds his listeners that they are children of the prophets and of the covenant God made with Abraham, when He said that all the families of the earth should be blessed through his offspring.
The author refers to God's promise to Abraham, confirmed by an oath, to bless him and make his descendants numerous, as proof of God's unchangeable purpose.
Galatians explains the mechanism by which all nations are blessed in Abraham: through faith.
Refers directly to the fulfillment of the promise given to Abraham to become a great and numerous nation.
The basis of the promise: The name change to 'father of a multitude of nations' prepares for the blessing for all.
Confirms that Abraham's blessing and the promise are transferred to his descendants (Jacob).
The original giving of the promise to become a great nation and a blessing, as confirmed in 18:18.
A direct parallel to the promise to become nations and kings, given in the covenant of circumcision.
Explains the purpose of the promise: that Abraham's blessing should reach the Gentiles through Christ.
Refers to God's oath to Abraham as the foundation of the promise of blessing.
